title: Sleeping Safely While Surrounded by Enemies
overview: A king on the run from a revolt tells God how many people are against him, yet finds enough trust to sleep and to ask for rescue.

parts.label: Surrounded and mocked (vv. 1-2)
parts.note: The psalm's heading ties it to the time David fled Jerusalem when his own son Absalom led a revolt against him. His enemies keep growing in number, and the cruelest blow is their taunt that even God will not save him.

parts.label: God as shield (vv. 3-4)
parts.note: A shield was a soldier's main protection, and lifting up someone's head means restoring their dignity and hope after shame. God answers from Zion, the hill in Jerusalem where God was pictured as living, which stands out because David had just been forced to leave that city.

parts.label: Sleeping in danger (vv. 5-6)
parts.note: Lying down, sleeping and waking up safe while huge numbers want him dead shows how fully he trusts God to keep him. The figure of many thousands of attackers is a way of saying a vast crowd, not an exact count.

parts.label: A cry for rescue (vv. 7-8)
parts.note: He asks God to rise up and act, and the picture of hitting enemies in the face and breaking their teeth treats them as wild animals made harmless, a genuinely violent image. The Hebrew can be read as a request or as something God has already done, and the psalm ends by praying for blessing on the whole people, not just on David.

think: What, if anything, helps a person rest when it feels like everything is stacked against them?
